A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BLiM/CPN research. Their main text and Appendices A–G are complete and readable, supporting reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments, CPN decoding evaluations and ablations in Section 4, plus captioning, multi-text retrieval and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark comparisons and the additional experiments and case studies in Appendices E–G.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same model architecture, bidirectional training objectives, likelihood combination, CPN normalization and decoding, and two-stage retrieval procedure. The image-retrieval adaptation is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four main video-retrieval datasets, COCO/Flickr30K image retrieval, multimodal understanding and captioning benchmarks, MSVD/VATEX multi-text retrieval, and ReXTime instruction-based examples.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched experiments. In particular, MM-Embed, RagVL and LamRA remain in Table 3; the new related-work citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, dataset splits, model configurations, 16-frame video inputs, top-16 reranking and training settings remain unchanged. Appendix A and Table 8 retain the same sample counts and experimental settings.

E4.justification: The likelihood and CPN ablations in Tables 5, 7, 12 and 13, normalization sensitivity in Figure 10, prior-bias analyses and qualitative case studies are retained. No new analysis or robustness test is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate and correlation reporting, without repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Parenthesized values in Table 10 remain inference times.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, plotted trends and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains BLiM's DiDeMo R@1 values of 86.4 for text-to-video and 82.8 for video-to-text retrieval. Figure 11 changes labels, not outcomes.

T1.justification: Proposition 1, its assumptions, the proof in Appendix D and the method equations are unchanged. Correcting the video-prior notation in Figure 11 does not revise a mathematical definition or argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same BLiM/CPN contributions, novelty claim within MLLM-based text-video retrieval, claimed average 6.4 R@1 advantage and broader applicability claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of candidate-prior bias, the benefits of bidirectional estimation and CPN, and stronger textual-prior effects remain unchanged. Appendix E.4 retains the qualification that longer generated outputs can increase decoding overhead.

D1.justification: The model initialization, LoRA training, hyperparameters, eight-A6000 hardware setup and inference details remain the same in Section 4 and Appendix B. The code-availability statement and repository link are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds two Lin et al. papers as references 59–60 and explicitly acknowledges Visual-GPTScore as closely related work on language priors and debiasing. This replaces the short RagVL description, while retaining RagVL's reference and experimental comparison.

P1.justification: The MLLM-based retrieval paragraph in Section 5 receives a localized rewrite, accompanied by citation renumbering and version-header updates. The main narrative, section order and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 11(b) corrects both video-candidate-prior labels from P(t) to P(v), with small annotation-layout adjustments. The added references also reflow the bibliography; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 improves acknowledgment of closely related prior work in Section 5 and corrects misleading video-prior labels in Figure 11(b). Although the brief RagVL description is removed, its experimental comparison remains. These provide modest gains in research positioning and clarity without changing the scientific evidence.
